prompt: An application using a standard, non-cluster-aware Redis client sends commands to its Redis Cloud database endpoint and receives the replies above. What does this indicate?
explanation: MOVED tells the client that these keys map to a hash slot served by a different shard endpoint. This is expected when the database has the OSS Cluster API enabled, a Redis Cloud Pro option found in the Performance section of the configuration: clients must first fetch the cluster topology and then connect directly to the proxy on each node that hosts a master shard, so you must use a client that supports the cluster API. Under the default clustering setup, a single endpoint automatically routes every command to the right shard and no cluster-aware client is needed, which is why the application worked until the database was switched to the OSS Cluster API.
code:
> SET session:42 "abcdef"
(error) MOVED 9117 redis-12003.internal.c18.us-east1-mz.gke.cloud.rlrcp.com:12003
> GET session:42
(error) MOVED 9117 redis-12003.internal.c18.us-east1-mz.gke.cloud.rlrcp.com:12003

options.text: The database has the OSS Cluster API enabled, so the client must be cluster-aware and route keys to the shard endpoints that own their slots
TLS was enabled without updating the client's trust store, so commands are rejected
The database user's ACL role denies SET and GET
The public endpoint has been blocked, so only private endpoints accept traffic
